title: Taro pilé et sauce jaune (Pounded Taro with Yellow Sauce)
author: Maman Tonta (camer.be, ‘La recette du dimanche’)
desc: Taro boiled in its skin about 2 hours and pounded hot, served with a palm-oil sauce emulsified with rock salt and lukewarm water, seasoned with cubes and a flamed whole pepper, with beef tripe cooked about 1 hour.
longDesc: A French-language printing from the Cameroonian news site camer.be, credited to Maman Tonta of Bazou. The taro is boiled in its skin about 2 hours. Tripe is cooked with salt and onion about 1 hour. The palm oil is warmed gently to liquefy, the rock salt added, and the lukewarm water poured in while whisking; once the emulsion holds, the rock salt is removed. Cubes, tripe and a flamed whole pepper go in. The taro is peeled and pounded in a mortar while still hot (the page says cold it hardens) until smooth with no lumps, with a little water if it is too stiff.
ingredients: 50 grams condiments to dilute (the achu spice mix — contents not printed)
steps: Boil the taro in its skin, ‘en robe des champs’, about 2 hours.
Cook the tripe with salt and the onion for about 1 hour. Set aside.
Dissolve the condiments in enough water.
Warm the palm oil gently so it liquefies. Add the rock salt, then pour in the lukewarm water, whisking, until the emulsion is stable. Remove the rock salt.
Crumble in the cubes, add the condiments and salt, then add the tripe and the flamed whole chilli. Taste.
Peel the hot taro and pound it in a mortar until the paste is smooth. Moisten with a little water if too stiff. Serve with the sauce.
chefTips: Printed cue: ‘une fois que l’émulsion est stabilisée, ôter le sel gemme’.
Pound the taro while it is hot — cold, it hardens (printed).
The page does not name the condiments or give a final sauce cooking time.
commonMistakes: Leaving the rock salt in the sauce after the emulsion forms.
Adding all the water at once to the oil.
healthBenefits: Taro is the starch; tripe adds protein.
culturalNote: The page describes this as a special dish from the grand ouest of Cameroon (West, South-West, North-West) and credits Maman Tonta de Bazou. It is the best fully quantified West-region printing of this dish found in this research.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Le Taro pilé et sa sauce jaune’. Byline as printed: ‘Maman Tonta’ (contributor from Bazou). ‘Dimanche 23 août 2020 08:50’. Yield ‘4 personnes’. TWO-PASS for figures; first-pass method wording was a paraphrase.

ABSENT, not estimated: the identity of the ‘condiments à délayer’; final cooking time for the sauce; salt and chilli quantities. The cook figure (120) is the printed taro time; the tripe (60) overlaps and is not added.
